text:
miranda_sales: Hi team — HealthComms (enterprise POC) wants a Private/VPC setup to call our private inference endpoint from their on-prem EHR cluster. They asked whether we should do Transit Gateway peering or PrivateLink. They also want a recommended minimal firewall allowlist + an estimate of any extra pricing impact for PrivateLink. Can ops/infra weigh in?
ryan_net: Short answer: both can work. TGW peering (transit) gives L3 connectivity and preserves source IPs; PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is L3 over ENIs but looks like inbound from our VPC IPs — so you lose original src unless customer uses proxy headers.
amos_solutions: For a POC I'd normally recommend PrivateLink when customers want strict isolation and no route table changes across accounts. TGW/peering is better for full mesh and if they need to run stateful firewalls on-prem.
anita_sec: A couple security notes: PrivateLink limits exposure to specific services (good). But confirm whether HealthComms' security team requires TLS inspection or will allow our certs. If they do TLS inspection, we need to confirm SNI preservation + cert pinning implications.
sophie_sales: Miranda — they also asked about port restrictions. HealthComms is very strict: only 443 outbound allowed. Is that fine?
ryan_net: 443 is fine for TLS. If you go PrivateLink, we provide interface endpoints in our account that will have ENI IPs in their VPC (or we ask them to create endpoints in their account pointing to our service). The allowlist they'd put on their firewall would be our endpoint ENI IPs (CIDRs) or our NAT EIP depending on topology.
miranda_sales: Can you paste a minimal allowlist snippet they can pass to their NetSec team? They asked for a single-line example and a CIDR range if possible.
ryan_net: Sure — minimal suggestions: 
```
# Allow outbound TLS to Redwood Private endpoint
source: 10.10.0.0/16  # customer app subnet
dest: 10.255.32.0/28  # example interface endpoint ENIs (replace with actual)
ports: 443/tcp
protocol: tcp
```
Note: For TGW transit you'd instead allow to our spoke CIDR (we can publish per-account ranges) or to NAT EIPs if using internet egress.
amos_solutions: Also include these notes for their OWASP/SecQA: PrivateLink is cross-account and supports VPC endpoint policies. We recommend an endpoint policy limiting actions to sagemaker-like/llm inference service action names (or our specific API verbs).
anita_sec: Add: Audit logs will show ENI flow logs. If they require full visibility, ask them to enable VPC Flow Logs on the endpoint subnets.
miranda_sales: Pricing question: what extra will we bill for PrivateLink vs TGW? They wanted an estimate for the POC.
sophie_sales: For POC pricing estimate: PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint + per-GB data processing charges on cloud provider side (they pay cloud fees), and we may include a small per-GB handling surcharge for cross-account NAT if we provide EIPs. TGW transit tends to be cheaper for large sustained bandwidth but requires more network handoff work (and possibly longer lead times for internal approvals). I'll prepare numbers after infra confirms which cloud and region.
ryan_net: One more operational gotcha: MTU and path MTU can break larger payload streaming. For high-throughput inference, ensure their client TLS stack supports larger MSS or disable path-mtu fragmentation. We often recommend testing with a streaming session (1M tokens) in the POC.
miranda_sales: HealthComms also filled part of the security questionnaire asking whether we can provide a static source IP for allowlisting (they prefer a single NAT EIP). Is that possible?
amos_solutions: We can offer a static egress EIP per-customer if we run a NAT in a public subnet for the private deployment or use a proxy in their VPC for Hosted. For PrivateLink specifically, the cleanest is to have them peer to our service via interface endpoints so they don't need to depend on internet EIPs. But if they insist on a single IP, we can allocate an EIP and route through it — will add infra ops work and likely a small monthly fee.
anita_sec: If we provide a shared EIP, make sure it's single-tenant for enterprise customers (no other customers behind it) to satisfy audit.
sophie_sales: Miranda — I'll draft three short options for the quote: 1) PrivateLink + per-endpoint fees (fastest approval), 2) TGW peering (cheaper at scale, slower approval), 3) Static EIP/proxy (meets allowlist constraints, extra infra charge).
miranda_sales: Perfect. Can someone post a concise bullet list for the customer email summarizing tradeoffs + next steps? They want this within EOD.
ryan_net: Email-ready bullets: 
- PrivateLink: minimal routing changes, strong isolation, requires per-endpoint allowlist (ENI CIDRs); best for quick POC approvals.
- Transit Gateway / Peering: full L3 connectivity, preserves client IPs, better for broad integrations, may need network team's change windows.
- Static EIP / proxy: single IP allowlist for customer firewall, requires NAT/proxy provisioning and dedicated EIP (adds infra/setup fee).
Next steps: confirm cloud provider + region, whether HealthComms will accept ENI CIDR allowlist or needs single EIP, and whether TLS inspection is allowed. I'll run a quick endpoint IP inventory once they confirm.
miranda_sales: Thanks — I'll send that and push for cloud/region.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: create-ppoc-endpoint ticket #POC-4821 created and assigned to @amos_solutions. ETA 2 business days for endpoint IPs and security artifacts.
miranda_sales: Awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
